name: Mas de la Pyramide

dates.note: No construction date is recorded, because no source read here states one. The commune's own page dates neither the mas nor the caves; the museum literature says the site gathers « plus de trois siècles de vie et de métiers agricoles », which is a span of occupation and not a date of building.

refs.title: Reportage de France 3 sur le Mas de la pyramide – Ville de Saint-Rémy-de-Provence
refs.note: The commune's own page, read as continuous prose. It says the mas is « à la fois musée rural dans des grottes et en même temps une incroyable ferme troglodytique toujours habitée », that the « pyramide » is « en fait une colonne naturelle de pierre dressée à plus de 20 m de hauteur, qui témoigne du travail de taille », and that the owner Lolo Mauron « vient d'en faire don à la commune de Saint-Rémy-de-Provence » -- so ownership has changed since the node's exemplar was written.

refs.title: Musée Agraire du Mas de la Pyramide à Saint-Rémy de Provence: guide, avis, infos pratiques, plan
refs.note: A tourism guide, carried only as a second surface for the identification of the site between Glanum and Saint-Paul-de-Mausole. Not an authority for anything architectural.

note: Tranche 3, French manoir and provincial farmhouse cluster, 5 Sep 2026. NO SURVEY AND NO MEASUREMENTS, and the reason is worth stating: repeated searches of the Base Mérimée found no notice for this building. It is not a monument historique and it has not been studied by the regional Inventaire under a name this cluster could find, so the only locators are the commune's own page and tourism literature. The node names it for the clearest demonstration that a Provençal farm is built out of, and into, its own quarry; that reading is the node's and is not sourced by anything quoted here.
